memories.title: Query-time tool perf: arch/search/query fixes on large repos (modernc)
memories.body:
Benchmarked LLM-facing graph tools on HotChocolate (8.8k files, 124k symbols, 405k edges, 626MB store) under modernc (pure-Go sqlite, 3-5x slower than C sqlite3 — ALWAYS measure under modernc, not system sqlite3).

Three query-time wins (all algorithmic, help every call cold or warm; proved byte-identical to old code by diffing old vs new binary on the SAME store — unit tests alone did NOT catch a regression):

1. get_architecture: 3.4s -> 0.82s (4.2x). Root cause was TWO things: (a) the deps SQL was a 4-way join over 405k edges keyed on 32-char TEXT UUIDs grouped by full path strings; replaced with a join-free streaming scan `SELECT file_id, dst_node_id FROM edges WHERE src_node_id IS NOT NULL AND dst_node_id IS NOT NULL` and resolve dst file via an in-Go nodeId->fileId map (ed.file_id already IS the src file). (b) moduleOf() is O(roots) longest-prefix scan (345 roots) called per-file AND per-dep-row (~80k times = ~1.6s of Go). Fix: build fileId->module map ONCE. Also folded per-file symbol counts + nodeId->fileId into a SINGLE nodes scan.

2. search_graph candidate exact pass: 373->195ms. `lower(n.name) IN (...) OR lower(n.qualified_name) IN (...)` couldn't use idx_nodes_name (lower() wraps the column) -> full 124k-node scan. Added expression indexes idx_nodes_lname/lqname (migration v15, additive, no graph wipe; build cost ~0.4s, no indexing regression) and split the OR into two index-seekable arms merged/sorted in Go (an OR across two columns defeats both indexes).

3. query_graph edge filter: 503->167ms (3x). `n.id IN (SELECT src/dst_node_id FROM edges WHERE kind=?)` scanned all edges into a temp list; replaced with correlated `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM edges ed WHERE ed.dst_node_id=n.id AND ed.kind=?)` riding idx_edges_dst / idx_edges_src(...,kind).

GOTCHA hit: when reordering a WHERE clause to put `IN (...)` before `worktree=?` for index use, you MUST reorder the bound args to match (placeholders are positional). A mis-bind returned 0 rows but unit tests passed because the split/lexical fallback still surfaced the target — only an old-vs-new diff on real data caught it.

Remaining slowest: arch 0.82s (two unavoidable full scans of 124k nodes + 287k edges through modernc) and FTS bm25 over common terms (e.g. "schema"). The deepest remaining lever across ALL tools is the TEXT-UUID primary keys -> integer rowids (smaller store, far cheaper joins/scans), but that's a high-risk schema refactor.</body>

memories.title: Search demotes generated files (graphql codegen, .pb.go, .min.js)
memories.body: Generated-file symbols flooded search: on Ordia, graphql codegen was 38% of results (75% for 'product'). internal/graph/generated.go isGeneratedPath (path-based: /generated/ & __generated__ segments, .generated. infix, zz_generated prefix, .pb/.g/.designer/.min suffixes) + demoteGenerated stably sinks them below hand-written results without dropping any. Wired into all 3 SearchGuided finalizers. Exact candidate_symbols hits are protected from demotion (preserves 'agent guess wins'). Result: noise 38%->5.6%, zero recall loss.

memories.title: get_architecture must be budgeted; was unbounded (90k tokens on HotChocolate)
memories.body: MCP get_architecture returned EVERY module and EVERY inter-module dep edge. On graphql-platform (331 modules) that was 4404 dep edges = 351594 bytes ≈ 90k tokens in ONE tool call — and CLAUDE.md tells agents to 'orient first' with it. Fix (internal/mcp/graph.go budgetArchitecture): cap modules (by symbol count) and deps (by ref count) to limit=80 default, keep name order within the kept subset, add module_count/dep_count/truncated, add Limit input; scope stays the drill-down. Result 351594→11212 bytes (96.8% less). Session-start (agents/format.go) already capped at 8/8 so was unaffected. Verified no regression on Ordia (8 mod/11 dep, under cap): module+dep lists byte-identical to old binary, truncated=false, only +36B for the two total fields. Also round search/recall Score to 4dp (roundScore) — display-only, applied after sort so order is provably unchanged.

memories.title: Added search_content (graph grep): full-text search with enclosing-symbol context
memories.body:
The biggest gap forcing an LLM back to the external grep tool was that recarto had no full-text/content search: search_graph only matches symbol NAMES (identifier-tokenized), so literals, error/log message strings, config keys, magic constants, attribute/annotation usages, comments, and call sites inside method bodies were unfindable — verified on graphql-platform (the literal "maximum allowed execution depth" returned only name-tokenized near-misses, never the actual line).

Fix: new Engine.SearchContent (internal/graph/content.go) + MCP tool search_content + CLI `graph grep|content`. It scans the worktree's indexed files (files table → read from disk, so always fresh, no index bloat — graph stays rebuildable), regex (RE2) or literal substring, ignore_case, path_glob, language filter. Each match is annotated with its ENCLOSING symbol (kind + qualified_name) via nodes byte-ranges (fileSpanSet.innermostAt) — strictly better than grep, which returns bare path:line:text. Generated-file matches are demoted (reuse isGeneratedPath); output token-budgeted (Limit 50, MaxPerFile 5, line cap 240).

Perf: whole-file re.Match pre-filter before line-splitting → 1.34s→0.39s (3.4x) over 8849 files on graphql-platform (modernc pure-Go sqlite).

Token win: for a literal query grep gives raw lines and the LLM must open each file to learn which method/class the hit is in; search_content gives that inline in one call, eliminating follow-up Read/get_code_snippet round-trips. Lets the LLM stay entirely inside recarto for codebase search. No regressions: full suite green, purely additive.

memories.title: Search dedup by qualified name, not bare name (fixes "find all definitions of X")
memories.body:
The single biggest grep-fallback gap in graph search: `dedupByName` collapsed every result sharing a bare symbol name to ONE entry. On graphql-platform, `graph search ExecuteAsync` returned 1 of 298 distinct ExecuteAsync methods — useless for "find all implementations/definitions of X", forcing a fall back to grep (3610 hits across 545 files).

Fix (internal/graph/search.go): replaced `dedupByName` with `dedupBySymbol`, keyed by `symbolKey()` = lowercased qualified_name (Namespace.Type.Method), falling back to name+path when no qualifier exists. This folds (a) the same node reappearing across FTS passes and (b) true overloads within one type, while preserving genuinely distinct same-named symbols across types. Applied at all 3 dedup sites + mergeHybrid's inline dedup.

After: `ExecuteAsync` returns 20 distinct qualified definitions (IRequestExecutor, DefaultRequestExecutor, IConnection, ...). A/B vs baseline over 12 NL concept queries: top-1 identical on all; "validate" 15→20 (surfaces the real SchemaValidator/DocumentValidator/Fusion validators instead of collapsing them + padding with test methods). No regression — bm25 ranks before dedup, so higher-relevance symbols still lead; only lower-ranked same-symbol dupes fold. Locked by TestSearchReturnsDistinctSameNameDefinitions.

memories.title: find_implementations: query inheritance edges to answer "what implements X"
memories.body:
Second-biggest grep-fallback in OO codebases: "find all implementations/subclasses of interface X". search_graph can't answer it — implementers (DefaultRequestExecutor) don't share the interface's name (IRequestExecutor). The graph already records `extends` edges (12,664 on graphql-platform) for `class C : Base, IFoo`; nothing exposed them.

Added Engine.Implementations (internal/graph/hierarchy.go): direction "down" (default) returns subtypes/implementers, "up" returns supertypes. Matches the query type by bare OR qualified name; down-edges also match the edge's recorded dst_name (not just resolved dst_node_id) so the ~10% unresolved inheritance edges still return. Exposed as CLI `graph impls <symbol> [--super]` and MCP tool `find_implementations`.

Validated on graphql-platform: `impls IRequestExecutor` → 5 implementers (ExecutorSession, DefaultRequestExecutor, RequestExecutorProxy, FusionRequestExecutor, StubExecutor) with qualified names + line numbers in ONE call; `impls ISchemaDefinition` → 4 (more complete than a `: ISchemaDefinition` grep regex, which missed one). `(no matches)` is a correct empty result (e.g. ISchema, which nothing implements), not an error. Locked by TestImplementationsFindsSubtypes (graph) + TestGraphImplementations (cli).

memories.title: trace callers/callees: aggregate ambiguous bare names + compact receivers (big grep-fallback fix)
memories.body:
LLM A/B testing on graphql-platform (8397 C# files) found `graph callers <bareName>` returned NOTHING for overloaded methods — the #1 grep-fallback. Root cause: nodeByName used LIMIT 1, arbitrarily picking ONE of 309 ExecuteAsync nodes (often one with zero incoming resolved candidates). Fix in internal/graph/trace.go: nodeByName→nodesByName returns ALL same-name matches (cap maxAmbiguousStarts=128); an exact qualified_name hit is preferred and returned ALONE (so qualified queries keep resolution precision — TestTraceCallPathCallersRespectsResolution still passes). callNeighbors now takes a frontier []string (IN clause) and the walk aggregates the first hop across every definition. Result: callers ExecuteAsync 12B→5004B answering vs rg 465KB.

Second fix: receiver expressions were dumped verbatim — 23226 call edges had multi-line receivers (max 5594 chars, fluent builder lambdas). compactReceiver() collapses whitespace + caps at maxReceiverLen=48. Applied at the scan site so both CLI and MCP trace_call_path benefit.

Third: `graph arch` CLI was unbudgeted (272KB on graphql-platform) — budgetArchitecture lived only in internal/mcp. Moved to graph.BudgetArchitecture (DefaultArchLimit=80); MCP keeps a thin wrapper; CLI now budgets + prints "showing 80/331 modules, 80/4404 deps" and accepts a path-scope arg. 272KB→9KB.</body>

memories.title: graph callers/callees: dedup identical rendered chains with (×N)
memories.body: LLM A/B on graphql-platform: 'graph callees DefaultRequestExecutor.ExecuteAsync' emitted 26 lines but only 7 unique (73% pure duplication). Cause: one ambiguous low-confidence call site keeps up to lowCapPerEdge=5 name-matched candidate target nodes; the CLI trace renderer omits per-hop paths, so the N distinct candidate nodes render byte-identical. Fix (internal/cli/graph.go callers/callees): collapse byte-identical rendered chains preserving first-seen order, append '  (×N)' when N>1 so the ambiguity count is reported not dropped. Result 26->7 lines / 2385->727 bytes (69% fewer tokens), higher signal. No graph-logic change so MCP JSON chains (which carry distinct paths) are untouched; zero test regression.

memories.title: find_annotated: query attribute/decorator usages (new grep-fallback fix)
memories.body:
LLM A/B on graphql-platform found a top grep-fallback with no graph answer: "find every symbol decorated with attribute X" (e.g. all `[ExtendObjectType]` classes, every `@Component`). search_graph returns only the attribute's *definition* + same-named methods; raw grep `\[ExtendObjectType` is noisy — it also matches the attribute's own def, doc comments, and string literals (e.g. Errors.cs `messageFormat: "Consider upgrading [ExtendObjectType<{0}>]..."`).

Fix: attributes nest INSIDE the decorated declaration's span in the C#/TS grammars, so an edge anchored at the attribute name resolves via enclosing() to the decorated symbol (innermost — member attr → method, class attr → class). Added a new `annotates` edge kind:
- parse: csharp.scm + typescript.scm capture `@reference.annotation` (identifier / qualified_name / generic_name for C#; identifier / call_expression / member_expression for TS decorators); edgeKind "annotation"→"annotates".
- graph.Annotated(wt, attr, limit): SELECT src nodes of annotates edges by dst_name; C# `Attribute`-suffix tolerant (matches attr, bare, bare+"Attribute").
- exposed as CLI `graph annotated <Attr>` + MCP tool `find_annotated`.
- store migration v16 resets graph cache so edges backfill on reconcile (bumped schemaVersion 15→16 + TestSchemaVersionIs16).

Result on graphql-platform: clean symbol-typed list (FQN + kind + loc), Errors.cs false-positive excluded, member-level + suffix tolerance verified. No regression: annotates is a separate edge kind, so search/trace/impls/content are untouched (spot-checked identical). See [[recarto-search-quality-tiers]].

memories.title: get_file_outline / graph outline: file structure without reading the whole file
memories.body:
LLM A/B on graphql-platform found a top Read/grep-fallback with NO graph answer: "what's in this file / give me the outline of file X." To understand a 428-line file (DefaultRequestExecutor.cs) an LLM had to Read all 13286 bytes. `arch <file>` only dumped global dep edges (no per-file symbols); `query` exposed Path in the engine but the CLI never surfaced it.

Fix: added `Engine.Outline(worktree, path)` (internal/graph/outline.go) — lists a file's nodes ordered by start_line with kind/name/qualified_name/parent_name/signature/start_line/end_line. Surfaced as CLI `graph outline <file>` and MCP tool `get_file_outline`. CLI prints the path ONCE as a header (repeating the ~75-char path per row was the bulk of output — the exact token cost the command avoids) then `[kind] signature  :line`, indenting nested members whose parent_name matches a sibling. Real win: outline of DefaultRequestExecutor.cs = 1276 bytes vs 13286 (90.4% reduction) and gives signatures + line numbers to then get_code_snippet the one symbol. MCP returns a hint distinguishing "no symbols" from the common absolute-path/relative-path mismatch. instructions.go, README, CLI help all updated.

Pattern (consistent with prior fixes find_implementations/find_annotated): identify the grep/Read fallback that has no structural answer, add a first-class graph command for it, advertise in instructions so the LLM reaches for it.

memories.title: Grep/search truncation transparency + type-trace steering (LLM A/B fixes)
memories.body:
LLM A/B on graphql-platform (124k symbols) found three cases where recarto silently pushed an agent back to shell grep/search:

1. search_content (`graph grep`) silently capped at 50 (real grep found 103 TODOs) — a grep replacement that hides matches gives false-complete answers. Fix: SearchContentWithMeta counts every matching line and returns ContentMeta{Total,Shown,Truncated,PerFileCapped}; SearchContent stays a thin wrapper (no caller churn). CLI prints "… showing N of M matches; raise --limit=/--max-per-file= or narrow --glob=/--lang="; MCP SearchContentOutput exposes total/truncated/per_file_capped. Counting continues past MaxPerFile (cheap: skip attribution after the cap) so Total is true.

2. Tracing a TYPE (class/interface/record) dead-ended on a bare single line — calls target its methods, not the declaration. Fix: CallNode now carries Kind (nodesByName selects n.kind); graph.IsTypeKind drives a steer to find_implementations (implementers) + search_content (references) in both CLI hint and MCP TraceCallPathOutput.Hint.

3. CLI `graph callers <miss>` discarded the engine's lenient suggestions and printed nothing. Fix: CLI uses TraceCallPathFiltered and prints "(no symbol named X)" + "did you mean: …" (parity with MCP).

search_graph/`graph search` also note a likely-truncated full ranked page. instructions.go now advertises search_content + the type-trace hint. Committed d1d6452 on feature/llm-e2e-test.

memories.title: snippet-by-symbol + CLI flag discoverability (LLM A/B fixes)
memories.body:
LLM A/B on graphql-platform (124k symbols) surfaced three grep/Read-fallback gaps, all fixed:

1. get_code_snippet / `graph snippet` required BOTH file and symbol. After a search you have the name, not the path, forcing a search→snippet round-trip + wrong-path errors. Added Engine.SnippetByName (internal/graph/snippet.go): file optional, resolves by name/qualified_name across the worktree. Unique → body; ambiguous → candidate list (path/line/qualified_name) so a qualified name (usually unique) disambiguates; miss → empty. Wired into CLI (`graph snippet <symbol>` single-arg) and MCP (File omitempty + Candidates output). Overloads sharing a qualified name in one file still list as candidates (graceful).

2. DISCOVERABILITY (user-flagged): `graph grep` already supported -r/--regex, -i/--ignore-case, --glob=, --lang= on engine+CLI+MCP — but `graph <sub> --help` treated --help as the search pattern, so a CLI agent couldn't learn the flags without reading source. Added isHelpToken/containsHelpToken + a const graphUsage block; `graph help` or `graph <sub> --help` prints it. MCP already documents these via jsonschema, so MCP agents were fine — the gap was CLI-only.

3. Type dead-end steering hint suggested `graph grep <Type>` (substring: matches NameFactory/GetName). Changed to `graph grep -r '\bName\b'` (word boundary). On IRequestExecutor this cut matches 1476→226 (84% fewer tokens), precise references.

instructions.go updated: get_code_snippet file-optional note + regex/word-boundary references tip. All tests TDD-first; full suite + vet + fmt green.</body>

memories.title: Post-edit reconcile latency, not search, was the LLM-efficiency gap (incremental resolve)
memories.body:
LLM A/B on graphql-platform (124k symbols, 300k call edges): recarto's search/trace/outline/grep already beat grep+Read on tokens. The real efficiency killer was LATENCY — the lazy reconcile on the read path ran a FULL-worktree Resolve on ANY single-file edit, so the first graph query after an edit blocked ~75s. Fixed with ResolveIncremental (internal/graph/resolve_incremental.go): re-resolve only edges in dirty files ∪ edges whose dst_name ∈ (old∪new) node names of dirty files; fall back to full Resolve when a dirty file's `extends`/`implements` set changes (the one case names can't bound — partial classes split decl/impl across files). Scoped call strategies are callStrategies mechanically rewritten via scopeStrategy() to drive from the affected-edge temp table.

Also made resolution DETERMINISTIC: the equal-confidence/equal-locality tiebreaks (call denormalize, resolveNonCallEdges, S5 cap) ordered by RANDOM node id, so two full indexes of identical code disagreed by ~7245 rows. Now order by (path, start_byte, id). This both gives reproducible builds AND lets incremental==full be proven byte-identical.

Proof: incremental reconcile after a 1-file edit == from-scratch full index, BYTE-IDENTICAL (1,768,259 edge/candidate rows, same sha256), at 4.3s vs ~75s (~17x). Tests: TestResolveIncrementalMatchesFullResolve, TestResolveIncrementalDirectVsFull. Commit a340530. Validation method worth reusing: id-independent signature (join candidates→nodes→files, key by path+qualified_name+start_byte) compared across two independent indexes.

memories.title: Search-ranking noise tiers + query/snippet footguns (LLM A/B fixes)
memories.body:
LLM A/B on graphql-platform (124k symbols, C#) found five grep/Read-fallback gaps, all fixed with TDD + verified no-regression:

1. NAMESPACE FLOOD (biggest): a concept query whose terms land in a namespace name (e.g. "query execution pipeline" → namespace HotChocolate.Execution.Pipeline) returned 20/20 identical [namespace] rows — each file's `namespace X;` is a distinct node with its own path, so symbolKey never deduped them and short dense bm25 docs ranked them top. Zero useful results. Fix: symbolKey keys container kinds (namespace) by name alone (fold per-file dupes); demoteNamespaces sinks them to bottom.

2. TEST CROWDING: 14/20 top hits on "type resolver" were *Tests methods. Added isTestPath (segment test/tests, *_test.go, *Tests.cs, *.test/.spec.ts) + demoteTests — sink tests below product code, never drop (recall preserved, all-test queries untouched). Now 0/10 tests in top-10; TypeReferenceResolver/SchemaBuilder lead.

3. Search ranking unified in reorderByValue = demoteNamespaces(demoteGenerated(demoteTests)). Tier order: product > tests > generated > namespace. protect (exact candidate_symbols) never demoted.

4. CLI `graph query <name>` was a footgun: positional arg[0] was read as KIND not name, so `query OperationExecutionMiddleware` returned nothing despite help saying "look up a symbol by name". Rewrote to flag-based (--kind/--name/--path/--lang/--edge/--limit) with bare positional = NameLike.

5. CLI `graph search` ignored --limit/--lang/--kind → unknown --flag=val was appended as a SEARCH TERM, silently corrupting results (--limit=10 matched "limit" in yarn.cjs). Added the flags.

6. SNIPPET ambiguity: `snippet Foo` bounced "ambiguous (2 defs)" when the only collision was a C#/Java type and its same-named constructor. collapseOwnedConstructors drops a constructor whose QN is <typeQN>.<name> when that type is also a candidate; genuine 2-type ambiguity still bounces.

Updated CLI help (graphUsage) + instructions.go search_graph bullet to state product>tests>generated>namespace ranking.</body>

memories.title: Four silent footguns that pushed agents to grep (LLM A/B fixes, commit 26468f5)
memories.body:
LLM A/B on graphql-platform (124k symbols, C#) found four cases where recarto returned a misleading empty/garbage result, eroding trust and forcing a grep/Read fallback. All fixed with TDD + verified on the real repo, no recall/ranking regression (commit 26468f5):

1. **Trace dead-end honesty** (TraceCallPathFiltered): a resolved symbol whose only callers/callees are already on the start frontier (self-recursion, or sibling overloads that only call each other) made `walk` append nothing → chains==0 → CLI rendered "(no symbol named X)" (false "doesn't exist"). Fix: when starts>0 but chains==0, emit a root-only chain [[rootLabel]]; multi-start virtual root now carries commonKind(starts) so type dead-ends stay detectable. CLI now says "(no callers found)" + grep steer; MCP returns root chain + search_content hint. Empty chains now ONLY means unknown symbol.

2. **Snippet overloads** (SnippetByName): overloaded method (same qualified_name AND same file) bounced with unfollowable "ambiguous; re-run with a qualified name or the file" → forced whole-file Read. Fix: isOverloadSet (same QN, dotted, same path) → overloadSnippet returns every body in one result, each prefixed `// path:line`, capped at maxOverloadBodies=10. New snippetAt() fetches a body by (path,start_line) since Snippet() is name-keyed LIMIT 1 and can't reach non-first overloads. Guard: requires same FILE so Go's a.Dup/b.Dup (same bare QN, different files) stay candidates.

3. **Space-form flags**: `--kind class` was swallowed as a positional (parser only matched `--flag=`), silently ignoring filter AND limit → flood of unranked generated-code noise. Fix: coalesceValueFlags() rewrites `--flag value`→`--flag=value` for known value-flags once at top of Graph(), before the switch. Triggers only on exact known flag names; boolean flags (-r/-i/--super/--up) untouched.

4. **impls/annotated flag corruption**: both build the query name via strings.Join(rest), so `impls IFoo --limit 5` searched for "IFoo --limit=5" → no matches. (My earlier "impls recall gap" on ISchemaBuilder/IType was THIS test artifact — impls works fine without the flag.) Fix: parse --limit=, skip any `-`-prefixed token instead of folding it in.

Method that worked: build the freshly-`make`'d ./releases/linux-amd64/recarto, run each graph subcommand on graphql-platform as an LLM would, and treat any empty/garbage result on a symbol that demonstrably exists as a bug. A standalone probe under the module (internal pkgs can't be imported from /tmp) calling TraceCallPathFiltered / dumping edges directly was decisive for root-causing chains==0 and confirming the extends edge existed.

Docs kept in lockstep: instructions.go agent block, get_code_snippet + trace_call_path MCP descriptions, graph CLI usage (overloads print together; flags accept either form; impls/annotated take --limit).

memories.title: Two more grep-fallback footguns fixed (snippet suffix + call direction), commit 8965c81
memories.body:
LLM A/B on graphql-platform (124k symbols, C#) found two more cases where recarto pushed an agent back to Read/grep. Both fixed TDD, no regression, commit 8965c81.

1. get_code_snippet / `graph snippet` rejected the Type.Method suffix form. trace/callers/callees resolve `DefaultRequestExecutor.EnrichContext` (via nodesByName's segment-boundary `%.suffix` LIKE), but snippet matched only the bare name or full qualified_name, so a name copied from a trace missed and forced a whole-file Read. Fix: SnippetByName AND Snippet(file,…) now use the same dotted-suffix LIKE + exact-match-preference as nodesByName. Bare names still never trigger a broad LIKE; ambiguous names still bounce with candidates.

2. callers vs callees used the same `→` glyph with opposite meaning. The engine roots every chain at the queried symbol, so callers rendered target→caller while callees rendered target→callee. An LLM reads `A → B` as "A calls B" and got the call direction backwards on callers — worse than grep. Fix: arrows now uniformly mean "calls" (left calls right). callers chains are reversed (outer caller → … → symbol) in the CLI; the MCP trace_call_path reverses callers chains too and both surfaces carry an explicit `legend`/header restating the direction.

Pattern reinforced: any identifier form one graph command emits MUST resolve in every other command; and any directional rendering must be self-describing per line so a quoted line can't be read backwards. Docs live in internal/agents/instructions.go (canonical block) + MCP tool descriptions in internal/mcp/server.go + CLI help in internal/cli/graph.go.

memories.title: Two no-arg footguns fixed: query whole-graph dump + bare search (commit 921a235)
memories.body: LLM A/B on graphql-platform (124k symbols, C#) found two more cases where recarto returned misleading output that pushes an agent back to shell grep. (1) `query`/`query_graph` with no filter dumped the first page of the whole graph ordered by qualified_name — ~50 lines of vendored/generated noise (yarn .cjs `$` functions) returned as success. Fixed at the engine via QuerySpec.IsEmpty() so CLI graph query AND MCP query_graph are both guarded by one check. (2) `graph search` with no terms and no --symbol printed bare "(no matches)" (reads as "repo is empty"); now a usage error pointing at `query` for filter-only lookups. TDD red→green, full suite + vet clean, no regression on filtered queries / term searches. Docs regenerated: instructions.go, query_graph MCP description, graph usage block. Most other graph subcommands were already well-tuned from prior A/B sessions (callers-of-interface steering, grep -r truncation honesty, callees ×N dedup all verified good).

memories.title: grep now covers the whole worktree, not just parsed code (commit 4df84c2)
memories.body:
LLM A/B on graphql-platform (124k symbols, C#) found the biggest remaining push-to-shell-grep gap: `graph grep` / search_content (SearchContentWithMeta in internal/graph/content.go) only scanned files in the `files` table (parsed code). Grepping a dependency in a .csproj, a key in a .json, a CI setting in .yaml, or a doc reference in .md returned a silent "(no matches)" — a false negative that bounced the agent to shell grep, defeating "keep codebase search in recarto".

Fix: when no --language filter is set, SearchContent enumerates the whole worktree via listSearchableFiles() — `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard -z` (honors .gitignore like ripgrep), with a filesystem-walk fallback (skipDir denylist) outside git. NO LangForExt filter, so config/build/docs/data files are reached. Matches in indexed code still carry their enclosing symbol; matches elsewhere render as "[file scope]" (new grepAnnot helper in cli/graph.go; MCP omits empty symbol/kind). Binary files skipped via binaryExt set + looksBinary() NUL sniff. A --language filter still scopes to indexed code of that language (unchanged path = no regression).

Perf on graphql-platform: worst case full-worktree scan (17k files, no match) ~1.8s; typical matched query <0.7s. TDD: TestSearchContentSearchesUnindexedTextFiles + TestSearchContentSkipsBinaryFiles (graph) and TestGraphGrepCoversUnindexedFiles (cli). Full suite + vet green. Updated instructions.go, mcp/server.go tool desc, mcp/graph.go language param doc, cli/graph.go help.

Did NOT add .snap demotion: path-sort keeps the first grep page clean and snapshots are legitimately searchable; left generated.go untouched to minimize regression surface.

memories.title: Session-start orientation map: rank modules by file count, demote tests (not alphabetical)
memories.body:
The session-start hook's "Code map" tier (formatSessionContext in internal/agents/format.go) used to take the FIRST archModuleLimit(=8) modules/deps in name order straight from Architecture(). Because Architecture() returns modules sorted alphabetically, on a large monorepo this surfaced pure noise: on graphql-platform the 8 shown were Abstractions, Abstractions.Tests, Adapters.Mcp, Adapters.Mcp.* etc. (7/8 test/tiny-adapter), and every dep was "Abstractions -> X" with count 1-5. The actual core modules (Types, Data, Fusion.Execution) never appeared. The tier bypassed BudgetArchitecture's highest-signal selection that get_architecture/CLI use.

Fix: new graph.MapArchitecture(arch, limit) used only by the session-start map. It ranks modules by FILE count (not symbols — symbol count is inflated by generated/codegen clients e.g. Nitro.Client = 23721 symbols in 43 files, which would crowd out hand-written modules) with test modules demoted below product modules; deps ranked by reference count with edges touching a test module demoted ("tests reference code under test" is the heaviest yet least informative edge). Then restores name order for stable display. isTestModuleName splits a module name on '/' and '.' and matches a whole test/tests segment (conservative: "testing"/"contest"/"CostAnalysis" don't match). BudgetArchitecture and the get_architecture tool are deliberately UNTOUCHED (no tool regression). Same token budget, far higher signal: graphql-platform now shows Types(992 files), Data, Fusion.Execution, CommandLine, Mocha + product->product coupling.</body>

memories.title: Augment hook (Grep/Glob) dedups repeated patterns per session
memories.body: handleAugment in internal/agents/handle.go re-injected a byte-identical symbol/bug block on every Grep/Glob, even for a pattern already searched in the same session — pure token waste (verified ~190 tok block re-emitted on graphql-platform "AddressLookup"). Fixed by mirroring the repeated-read suppression: key on ledger scope "session:"+SessionID, metric "augment:"+pattern. Peek before searching — if the pattern already injected content this session, suppress the block, bump lifetime/repeated_augments_blocked, and emit a one-line nudge ("You already searched ... rely on that injection"). Only mark the pattern as injected when content was actually produced AND SessionID is non-empty, so the reminder never fires spuriously and empty-result patterns can re-run later. Added repeated_augments_blocked to `recarto status` lifetime list. Tests: TestAugmentSuppressesRepeatedPattern, TestAugmentNoDedupWithoutSession. Did NOT touch the session-start map edge selection (deliberately reworked in ef47ac0) to avoid a regression.

memories.title: Session-start map backfills edge endpoints into the module list
memories.body: MapArchitecture (internal/graph/architecture.go) ranked modules by file count but edges by reference count, computed independently. On large monorepos a coupling hub (many refs, few files) anchors the heaviest edge yet falls out of the top-N module list, leaving "dangling" edge endpoints the agent has no context for. Cross-repo scan (rollout, ordia, recarto, wterm, ftui, pruna, go-updater, research-tool, world-game, graphql-platform) showed the defect is isolated: only graphql-platform had dangling edges (6 of 8; heaviest = ChilliCream.Nitro.Client→Types.Abstractions 7435 refs). Chose Option 2 (backfill) over filter/rerank because it's surgical: module set = top-N by files ∪ endpoints of shown edges. No-op on the 9 coherent repos (zero regression to the ef47ac0 ranking); on graphql-platform grows 8→13 modules so all 8 edges resolve. Endpoints with no Module entry are skipped (keeps existing dep-only tests green). Tests: TestMapArchitectureBackfillsEdgeEndpoints, TestMapArchitectureNoBackfillWhenCoherent. Methodology lesson: scan multiple repos before picking a map heuristic — the "obvious" filter option would have discarded the single most important edge on the one repo that needed help.

memories.title: Augment hook reduces file globs to identifier stem, skips stemless ones
memories.body: handleAugment (internal/agents/handle.go) fed the raw Grep/Glob pattern into graph.Search as a symbol query. A file glob like `*.cs` degraded to the literal "cs" and injected minified-bundle noise (functions named `cs`, `Cs.u`) on every glob — token waste + misleading. Fix: augmentSearchTerm (internal/agents/augment.go) classifies the pattern. Non-glob Grep terms ("AddProjection", "Add.*Projection", "foo*") pass through byte-identical (no regression). File globs reduce to the longest identifier run of the basename minus extension/wildcards (`**/*Projection*.cs`→"Projection"). Pure-extension/stemless globs (`*.cs`, `src/**/*.go`, `internal/**`) return ok=false → handleAugment injects nothing. looksLikeFileGlob is narrow (needs `**`, or `/`+wildcard, or wildcard-basename-ending-in-.ext) so regexes are never misclassified. Verified on graphql-platform: `*.cs` now injects nothing; `*Projection*.cs` returns real Projection symbols.

memories.title: Session-start map demotes edges dominated by generated-source refs
memories.body: The session-start code map's deps were dominated by codegen: a generated GraphQL client (ChilliCream.Nitro.Client/Generated/ApiClient.Client.cs, ~23k symbols) produced edges like `Nitro.Client → Types.Abstractions (7435)` that crowded out product coupling AND, via edge-endpoint backfill, dragged generated client modules into the module list. Fix: ModuleEdge gained GeneratedFrom (subset of Count whose source file isGeneratedPath), populated in Engine.Architecture from srcf.path. MapArchitecture (internal/graph/architecture.go) demotes genDominatedEdge (GeneratedFrom*2 > Count) below genuine edges — after test-edge demotion (outer key), before count. Backfill then stops pulling generated endpoints. get_architecture/BudgetArchitecture is untouched (still ranks deps by Count). Verified on graphql-platform: map now leads with Fusion/Core/Types/Data product coupling; Nitro.Client + StrawberryShake dropped from the list.

memories.title: Read/edit hooks surface file-anchored do_not_repeat+decision just-in-time, deduped per session
memories.body:
The post-read/post-edit hooks (internal/agents/handle.go) used to surface only bug + todo memories anchored to the touched file. do_not_repeat (guardrail) and decision (rationale) memories only appeared in the budgeted session-start baseline, so the highest-signal guidance failed to fire at the point of change.

Fix: added memory.GuidanceForCode (internal/memory/guidance.go) returning do_not_repeat+decision anchored to refs, built on a new shared memoriesForCodeByKinds helper that also now backs BugsForCode/TodosForCode (collapsed three near-identical query bodies). handlePostRead/handlePostEdit surface guidance via formatGuidance (🚫 do-not-repeat, 📌 prior decision in internal/agents/format.go). Added dedupSurfaced in handle.go: per-session, per-memory-id ledger dedup applied to bug/guidance/todo surfacing so a memory re-found on every read/edit of the same code injects once per session instead of every touch — net token win even as coverage widens. learning/preference deliberately excluded from the just-in-time tier to keep precision high (they belong to recall). Instructions updated to teach agents to anchor memories to refs. Verified end-to-end on graphql-platform.</body>

memories.body: recarto init re-runs now upgrade existing agent integrations in place, not just add-if-absent. Claude hooks: settings.json hooks are recognized as recarto-owned by command grammar `<binary> hook <event> --agent claude` (isOwnedCommand in claudecode/settings.go — binary-path-independent, so renamed events / moved binaries get pruned). syncHooks() no-ops when the owned set already equals current hookSpecs, else prunes all owned hooks (removeOwnedHooks: drops empty groups, preserves foreign hooks) and re-adds the current set. memories.title: Session-start dedups the just-in-time read/edit tier
memories.body: handleSessionStart now marks the IDs of memories actually rendered into the session-start block (formatSessionContext returns them) as surfaced in the session ledger, via markSurfaced. dedupSurfaced already keys per-id, so the post-read/post-edit just-in-time hooks no longer re-inject a guardrail/bug/todo the agent can already see in the session-start block — duplicate context = token waste. Memories DROPPED under budget at session-start stay unmarked and still surface just-in-time, so no quality regression (verified by TestSessionStartDoesNotSuppressDroppedGuidance + the cross-session E2E check on graphql-platform).

memories.title: Post-read hook nudges toward the graph on large whole-file reads
memories.body: handlePostRead (internal/agents/handle.go) now emits a just-in-time nudge when an agent reads a large, graph-indexed file whole — previously the dominant token sink got zero advisory output (e.g. graphql-platform's TypeResources.Designer.cs cost ~39.5k tokens, silent). On the FIRST read of a file this session (n==1) whose ToolResult clears largeReadThreshold() (default 2000 tokens, override RECARTO_LARGE_READ_TOKENS, in format.go), it calls a.Graph.Outline(worktree, rel) and, when the file has >=1 symbol, appends a ~40-token nudge with the symbol count pointing at get_file_outline / get_code_snippet, and increments lifetime large_reads_nudged (surfaced in `recarto status`, internal/cli/status.go). Gated to n==1 so a repeat read keeps the stronger "rely on the earlier read" warning and never double-injects; silent for small reads and for unindexed files (no graph alternative). Documented in the installed instructions (instructions.go) so the nudge reads as a known guardrail. The nudge fires post-hoc (tokens already spent on that read) but steers the rest of that file's navigation to the graph. Tested in handle_test.go (positive, small-read, unindexed, once-per-file).

memories.title: Augment hook dedups bug surfacing against the per-session set
memories.body: handleAugment (internal/agents/handle.go) used to render concept-matched bugs straight from recall, bypassing the per-memory dedup (dedupSurfaced/markSurfaced) that the read/edit hooks use. So the same bug got injected twice in one session: shown at session-start or on a read, then re-injected by a later Grep/Glob, or surfaced by a search then re-injected on the next read of its file — pure token waste. Fix: collect the KindBug records from the recall, run them through dedupSurfaced (keyed by memory id, the same protocol post-read/post-edit use), build a `fresh` id-set, and render only survivors — preserving r.Caveat() by iterating set.Results. dedupSurfaced also marks survivors so a later read/edit stays quiet about a bug the search just showed. Passthrough when SessionID is empty (TestAugmentNoDedupWithoutSession). Symbol-search augmentation is unchanged. Tests: TestAugmentDedupsBugAlreadySurfacedOnRead + TestPostReadDedupsBugAlreadySurfacedByAugment.

memories.title: Code map module names use shortest-unique-suffix, dropping generic "src" wrapper
memories.body: moduleNames (internal/graph/architecture.go) previously fell back to the FULL relative path on a basename collision, so a monorepo like graphql-platform rendered modules as "src/HotChocolate/Core/src/Types" — repeated ~6x across the session-start code map and dozens of times across get_architecture. Now a colliding basename is named by the shortest trailing path suffix that is unique within the colliding group, after dropping generic wrapper segments (genericNameSegments = {"src"}) via cleanNameSegments; shortestUniqueSuffix computes the suffix. Result: "Core/Types", "MongoDb/Types", etc. Safety: if dropping "src" would make two distinct roots collapse to the same cleaned segments, the whole group falls back to full paths (never silently merges modules). Unique basenames are unchanged (bare basename). Measured on graphql-platform: get_architecture -10.7% (~240 tok), session-start map ~-10%, zero recall/uniqueness loss. Fix is in the shared Architecture() builder so session-start map, get_architecture, and graph arch all benefit. Tests: TestModuleNamesCollisionUsesCompactSuffix / ...FallsBackWhenCleaningWouldMerge / ...UniqueBasenameStaysBare in architecture_test.go.

memories.title: List tools drop redundant name, keep qualified_name as canonical id
memories.body: canonicalIdentifier (internal/mcp/graph.go) removes the short `name` from every list result (search_graph, query_graph, get_file_outline, find_implementations, find_annotated) whenever it is derivable from a non-empty qualified_name — either an exact copy (top-level funcs; multi-segment namespace nodes where name==qualified_name) or its trailing dotted segment (leafName). Empirically name is the leaf of qualified_name in 124428/124428 graphql-platform nodes across go/csharp/ts/tsx/js (separator is always '.'), so emitting both duplicated the leaf on every row. Name JSON tags are now omitempty; qualified_name is kept because it is the precise, overload-safe form get_code_snippet/trace_call_path/find_* already accept (verified: feeding a returned qualified_name back to get_code_snippet resolves found=true, no ambiguous-candidate round-trip). This makes MCP output match the CLI (which already shows only qualified_name) and cuts list-tool JSON ~7% (search) to ~10% (outline) with zero capability loss. The defensive branch keeps name when qualified_name is empty or name isn't its leaf so no row loses its only identifier. Instructions (internal/agents/instructions.go) updated to tell agents to read qualified_name (last segment = short name) and not expect a separate name field.

memories.title: recall: explicit kind filter is authoritative; §9.2 pin always-include scoped to unfiltered recall + dedicated sub-budget
memories.body:
Decision (LLM-consumer call, ratified by maintainer) resolving recarto feedback 019ea328.

CHANGE: In Engine.Recall (internal/memory/recall.go), an explicit `kind` filter is now AUTHORITATIVE — pinned do_not_repeat are filtered like any other kind (removed the isPin bypass). memories.title: Resolve speedup #2: shared S2/S4 prefix + drop dst-index during inserts + truncate clear
memories.body:
Second round of `recarto index` resolve-phase optimization (after the CROSS JOIN / parent_name / tb-index round). All changes in internal/graph/resolve.go, proven BYTE-IDENTICAL on graphql-platform (digest 3833f4c9…, candidates 885620 / call_resolved 194064 / noncall 13413 unchanged; from-scratch index counts identical too).

Root cause found by profiling each resolve sub-step on the real store (harness internal/graph/resolvebench_test.go, env RECARTO_BENCH_STORE): the typed-receiver (S2) and interface (S4) strategies BOTH recomputed an identical, dominant prefix — the files→edges→src(node bytes)→type_bindings scope-containment join over all ~167k receiver calls (~14s each). S5 name-fallback (window+786k inserts) and the per-edge candidate clear were the other costs.

Fixes:
1. **Shared recv_types temp table** (buildReceiverTypes): materialize the (edge→bound type) prefix ONCE, DISTINCT; S2/S4 read it as stratTypedReceiverShared/stratInterfaceShared. S2 16.9s→0.45s, S4 16s→0.7s, prefix paid once ~14.5s. Net ~−15s.
2. **Drop idx_edge_candidates_dst for the duration, rebuild once at end**: no resolve query uses it (PK (edge_id,dst_node_id) + edge_id seeks only). clear 6→2.3s, S5 22→17.6s, rebuild only 1.3s.
3. **Single-worktree clear = `DELETE FROM edge_candidates` truncate** (vs per-call-edge IN-subquery probe): 25.7s→2.3s on re-resolve. Multi-worktree keeps the filtered delete.
4. **clear-dst `AND dst_node_id IS NOT NULL`**: skips rewriting 300k already-NULL call edges on a first index (~2.9s→0).

Result: in-index resolve phase 68.6s→46.3s (−32%); total index 130s→105s. Re-resolve harness ~73→55s.

GOTCHAS (verified, do-not-repeat): (a) reordering the prefix to edges→type_bindings→src is SLOWER (14.5→29.5s): receivers usually match a binding name and a (file,name) has several bindings, so src is then looked up per-binding not per-edge. (b) my S4 "seek m by name before contains" reorder was 2× slower — common method names fan out worse than walking a specific type's members. (c) Incremental resolve (resolve_incremental.go) still uses the inline callStrategies via scopeStrategy's fromAnchor swap, so S2/S4 MUST keep an inline (files→edges) form — recv_types versions are full-Resolve only. (d) Headline wall-time on this box swings ±20% with page-cache warmth; trust the per-step Profile and digest, and use -count=1 (go test caches results).

See [[indexing-perf-resolve-bottleneck]].

memories.title: Resolve speedup #3: recv_types/S5/denormalize moved from SQL to in-memory Go
memories.body:
Third round of `recarto index` resolve-phase optimization (after CROSS-JOIN/parent_name/tb-index, then shared S2/S4 prefix). The full `Engine.Resolve` (internal/graph/resolve.go) ran three operations SQLite does worst; all three were moved into in-memory Go passes that load the worktree graph into maps (the whole graph fits in RAM) and emit a BYTE-IDENTICAL candidate set — verified via resolvedDigest in resolvebench_test.go (gated on RECARTO_BENCH_STORE).

What moved to Go (S1–S4 LIKE/qualified_name matching deliberately LEFT in SQL — its semantics, incl. SQLite case-insensitive LIKE with `_`/`%` wildcards, aren't worth reproducing):
- buildReceiverTypes: the interval-CONTAINMENT join (tb.scope_start<=src.start AND src.end<=tb.scope_end) SQLite can't index; a hot (file,receiver-name) bucket held up to 2,880 bindings so each call scanned the whole bucket. Bucket type_bindings by (file_id,name) once, test each receiver call against only its bucket. 18.1s→1.5s. Output still a TEMP TABLE `recv_types` the unchanged SQL stratTypedReceiverShared/stratInterfaceShared read.
- resolveNameFallback (S5): replaces stratNameFallback's PARTITION-BY window sort over ~786k rows. Same global hyper-common-name skip (>50 callables), language family, per-edge locality order + 10-cap, confidence-by-count (0.45 unique / 0.2 ambiguous). 23.2s→6.4s (now floored by the 786k-row INSERT).
- denormalizeBestCandidate: replaces ~300k correlated scalar subqueries. Pick each edge's best (confidence DESC, same-file, same-top-dir, mf.path, start_byte, dst id) in one in-memory pass. KEY: per-row UPDATEs were SLOWER than the original (12.2s); stage winners in a temp table + single bulk UPDATE → 5.0s. Relies on the preceding clear having NULLed every call edge, so only resolved edges are written.

Real first-index resolve on graphql-platform (8.8k files, 124k nodes, 435k edges, 885k candidates): 49.2s→21.0s (2.34x). Committed ba8dd10.

Gotchas baked in: (1) the single WriteTx connection can't read+write concurrently — drain every cursor (helper `scan`) before the insert loop; (2) topDir/sameLangFamily Go helpers replicate substr(path,1,instr(path,'/')) and the web-family {ts,tsx,js} scoping exactly; (3) DISTINCT in recv_types is (edge,type) since edge→dst_name/ef_language is functional. Incremental resolve (resolve_incremental.go, per-edge SQL via callStrategies) is untouched and still uses the strat constants. Measure under modernc (the bench test / real binary), not system sqlite.

memories.title: Index parse+write speedup: build graphs in workers, O(n) qualifiedName, decouple pipeline
memories.body:
After the resolve-phase work, the full `recarto index` was WRITE-BOUND: the single serial writer (indexWorklist's flush loop) spent ~50s on graphql-platform while 8 parse cores idled. Diagnosis via env-gated phase timing (RECARTO_PHASE_TIMING, since removed): writer 50s vs parse(sum) 30s/8≈4s effective; user/real≈1.2x (near-serial). Three fixes (commit 932f381), all in internal/graph:

1. **Build the file graph in the parse worker, not the writer.** Split writeFileGraph: new `buildFileGraph(src, res) fileGraph` (index.go) produces the full insertable row set (nodeRow/edgeRow/bindingRow/containsRow — ids and internal refs generated in the worker; only file_id bound at write time) and runs in the parallel pool; `writeFileGraph` now only upserts the files row and runs the prepared INSERTs. Moved ~22s of CPU (qualifiedName/ftsText/signatureOf/ids.New/enclosing) off the serial writer. parsedFile (reconcile.go) drops src/res, holds `graph fileGraph`.

2. **qualifiedName was O(n^2) per file** (rescanned every span per symbol for namespace prefixes AND walked the containment chain re-scanning). Three generated/vendored files (ApiClient.Client.cs 23467 symbols, two yarn .cjs 7600 each) pinned single workers for seconds → killed parallelism. Fix: precompute per file, once, `parentIdx[i]` (innermost container index via new `innermostContainerIdx` in graph.go — replaces `containingParent`, same innermost/first-on-tie rule) and `nsIdx` (namespace indices); qualifiedName now takes them and is O(namespaces+depth) per symbol. build CPU 22s→7s. The contains-edge loop also uses parentIdx.

3. **Pipeline stall:** the results channel was buffered to nworkers (8); the writer stopped draining it for the ~0.4s it held the lock per 128-file batch flush, so the pool filled 8 slots and stalled the rest of every flush (~half the wall idle). Fix: `resultsBuf := 4*indexBatchSize` so workers parse ahead while the writer flushes → serial writer becomes the sole floor.

Result: indexWorklist (parse+write) 54s→33s; full first index ~96s→~55s. Writer (~29s, ~1M inserts incl. 3 FTS tables) is the remaining floor — next lever would be drop/rebuild secondary indexes during a large bulk write (FTS can't be dropped/rebuilt cheaply).

VERIFICATION (no regressions): node ids are random UUIDv7, so the resolve digest can't compare across re-index. Used an **id-invariant content comparison** instead: index graphql-platform with baseline vs new binary, sha256 the structural content (path+spans+kind+name+qualified_name+parent_name+signature for nodes; type_bindings; edge structure via src/contains-child start_byte excluding resolved dst; nodes_fts_tri content via node identity) ordered deterministically — all four hashes IDENTICAL. Counts (nodes 124428/edges 435088/bindings 116572/candidates 885620/resolved-calls 194064) unchanged. Pattern: use sqlite3 CLI for id-invariant diffs of two real-indexed stores. Parsing itself parallelizes fine (microbench: 1→8 workers 1.63s→0.41s, ~4x on this 8-core box); it was never the bottleneck.

memories.title: Storage-engine benchmark: drop/rebuild indexes wins; cgo SQLite & PRAGMA tuning don't
memories.body:
Benchmarked SQLite alternatives for the index on a DEDICATED clean box (local was too noisy — a neighbor's tests made write(serial) swing 24–67s; lesson: benchmark on an idle machine, interleave configs back-to-back, take the ratio/min). Corpus: graphql-platform (8849 files, 124k nodes, 435k edges, 885,620 candidates), 4-core AMD EPYC, Debian 13, Go 1.26.4.

Full first index, write(serial) / resolve / total:
- baseline (modernc, pure-Go): 23.7s / 16.1s / 43.5s
- + PRAGMA tune (cache_size=-65536, temp_store=MEMORY, mmap_size=512M): 22.5 / 17.2 / 43.7 → WASH (−5% write, but tune slightly HURTS resolve; net nil). Dropped.
- + drop/rebuild 11 secondary indexes on fresh large index: 14.2 / 16.1 / 38.3 → WIN: −40% write, resolve neutral, −12% total. SHIPPED (commit 415f1d3, internal/graph/bulkload.go + reconcile.go).
- cgo C-SQLite (mattn/go-sqlite3, -tags "cgosqlite sqlite_fts5"): write 16.2s alone (−32%), 10.2 with the index trick (−57%) — genuinely faster writes. BUT resolve FAILS: "no such column: edges.file_id" — mattn rejects the correlated edges.file_id subquery in resolveNonCallEdges' UPDATE that BOTH modernc AND system sqlite3 3.46.1 accept (verified: same SQLite version, mattn-specific compile quirk, reproducible on clean box). So a full index can't complete under cgo without a SQL rewrite, plus the cgo toolchain (gcc, cross-compile) burden the CI already fights. NOT adopted.

Conclusions for "should we switch off modernc/SQLite": NO net win available by swapping. The remaining bottleneck is ~1M tiny FTS-indexed FK-checked concurrent inserts — SQLite's wheelhouse, where DuckDB (OLAP, bad at small writes) and KV stores (no SQL/FTS/joins — full rewrite) lose. modernc+index-trick (pure-Go, 38.3s, fully working) beats plain cgo (16.2s write but broken). The real levers are reducing WHAT is written (FTS tiers, candidate materialization), not the engine.

Method/infra notes: built a tag/env-driven harness (store_driver_modernc.go/store_driver_cgo.go via //go:build cgosqlite; RECARTO_TUNE/RECARTO_BULK/RECARTO_PHASE_TIMING env toggles) — all reverted before the final commit; the shipped change is ONLY the drop/rebuild path. The drop/rebuild index list is hardcoded (it's also the crash self-heal source so can't be captured at drop time) and guarded against migrate.go drift by TestGraphSecondaryIndexListMatchesSchema.

memories.title: Perf root causes: stat-less planner inverts trace IN(128) join (21s); serial grep; per-call arch recompute; row-by-row resolve writes
memories.body: Profiling on the dedicated box (graphql-platform, 8849 files / 124k nodes / 435k edges / 886k edge_candidates, 786k of them method='name'): (1) `graph callers ExecuteAsync` 21s — with 128 ids in the IN list and NO sqlite_stat1 (ANALYZE never runs on the store) the planner drives files→nodes→edges→edge_candidates, enumerating every call edge with B-tree seeks (17s in BtreeIndexMoveto/memcmp); only 229 ec rows actually match. Single-id IN uses idx_edge_candidates_dst and takes 2ms. Fix = CROSS JOIN forced order (codebase convention) and/or planner stats. (2) grep regex 2.3s = serial scan + Go regexp whole-file Match per file. (3) arch 2.0s = per-call projectRoots WalkDir + 4-join GROUP BY over 435k edges + unmemoized O(roots) moduleOf per path (0.66s). (4) fresh index 32.9s = parallel parse ~7s wall OVERLAPPED with serial writer 10.9s, then serial Resolve 14s (S5 fallback inserts 786k rows one Stmt.Exec at a time = 3.4s; denormalize ~300k single-row UPDATEs ≈ 2s; S1-S4 SQL 3.8s). Writer+resolve serial SQLite is the wall floor, NOT parse.

memories.title: Never combine PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys with dropped child indexes during bulk load
memories.body:
Deferring FK checks (PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys=ON) to allow out-of-order bulk inserts is a quadratic trap: while deferred violations are outstanding, SQLite must settle its violation counter on EVERY parent-table insert by scanning the child table for rows the new parent key satisfies — and the bulk-load path (dropGraphSecondaryIndexes) drops exactly the child indexes (idx_edges_src etc.) that would make that scan a seek. Result: the batched writer (multi-row VALUES inserts) went from ~11s to >4 MINUTES on graphql-platform (124k node inserts × growing unindexed edges table). Fix: keep immediate FK enforcement and coordinate flush ORDER instead — graphInserters are manual-flush; when any buffer fills, flush ALL in dependency order (nodes before edges/contains). writeFileGraph buffers a file's children strictly after its nodes, so the ordered flush never writes a child before its parent.

**Why:** the failure is silent and only appears at scale (small test stores have indexes... no — they have tiny child tables), so tests stay green while production is 10× slower.
**How to apply:** for any future bulk path: either keep child indexes, or keep FK checks immediate and order the writes.

memories.title: Multi-row VALUES batching is a pessimization on modernc/sqlite — per-row prepared stmts in a tx are already optimal
memories.body: Benchmarked on the dedicated box (graphql-platform fresh index): replacing per-row prepared INSERTs with 200-row multi-VALUES batches made the serial writer SLOWER (10.9s → ~15s cum; whole index 32.9s → 37.8s; resolveNameFallback 4.5s → 5.0s). Profile: modernc stmt bind cost 5.6s for the big arg arrays + VALUES coroutine machinery; there is no per-call round-trip to amortize in an embedded driver — the per-row Exec overhead the batching was meant to remove was never the cost; actual btree+FTS work was. **Why:** multi-row INSERT batching is a client-server optimization (network round trips); embedded SQLite gains nothing and pays extra bind/coroutine cost. **How to apply:** for modernc write-path tuning, keep one prepared single-row stmt per table per tx; optimize by removing WORK (indexes dropped during bulk, fewer rows, fewer tables), not by batching statements. (Related trap: see the defer_foreign_keys do-not-repeat.)

memories.title: Query-path wins shipped: CROSS JOIN trace fix 21s→0.2s, parallel grep 6×, token-cached arch 13×, incremental post-edit resolve
memories.body: Shipped on feature/index-speed-improvements (bench box, graphql-platform corpus): (1) callNeighbors now CROSS JOIN-pins the trace neighbor join (driver = IN-constrained table) — `graph callers ExecuteAsync` 21,000ms→210ms; plan locked by TestCallNeighborsPlanDrivesFromConstrainedTable via EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN. Full Resolve now ends with PRAGMA analysis_limit=1000 + ANALYZE so stores finally carry sqlite_stat1. (2) search_content scans files in a NumCPU worker pool with a requiredLiteral (regexp/syntax-derived, conservative) bytes.Contains prefilter — grep regex 2330ms→375ms, literal 410→333ms; also FIXED a latent bug where the whole-file re.Match gate made ^-anchored patterns match nothing. (3) Architecture: Go-side edge aggregation (stream edges + node→file maps; no 4-join GROUP BY), memoized moduleOf, and a meta-table cache keyed by graph_token (+archCacheVersion) — 2000ms→712ms cold/153ms warm. (4) handlePostEdit uses Engine.ReindexFileIncremental (IndexFile + ResolveIncremental with the extends-signature fallback guard) instead of a FULL resolve per edit (~14s on big repos → sub-second). Verified: full go test suite + old-vs-new fresh-store dump diff (no UUIDs) + CLI query output diff on the bench box.

memories.title: Storage stays SQLite: slowness was plans/algorithms, not the engine; fresh-index floor is real btree+FTS work
memories.body: Evaluated "explore other storage engines" with profiles on the dedicated box: every user-facing slowness was a query-plan or algorithm problem, not a storage problem — callers 21s was a planner join inversion (fixed with CROSS JOIN, 100×), grep was a serial scan (parallelized, 6×), arch was recompute-per-call (cached, 13×), per-edit was an unnecessary full resolve (made incremental). The fresh-index serial floor (~33s on 4 cores: writer ~11s of btree+FTS tokenization, resolve ~14s) is real work any engine with equal query semantics would pay; replacing SQLite would mean rewriting the entire read layer (search/trace/arch/snippet/content) for at most the writer's share, with correctness risk dwarfing the gain. Prior session evidence: cgo sqlite and PRAGMA tuning don't win either; this session: multi-row batching is a pessimization. Next plausible index levers if ever needed (all semantic trade-offs): fewer FTS broadener tables, capping S5 candidate volume (786k of 886k rows), INTEGER PKs instead of TEXT UUIDs (store size + every join).

memories.title: Trim S5 name-fallback candidate bloat (89% of edge_candidates rows, 60%+ of store size)
memories.body: 786k of 886k edge_candidates rows on graphql-platform are method='name' (S5 low-confidence name-only fallback, ≤10 per edge + conf 0.45 unique / 0.2 ambiguous). They dominate store size (627MB store for a 679MB repo — ec table + its two indexes ≈ 157MB+) and a chunk of full-resolve time (~3.4s of inserts). Options to evaluate, each a semantic trade-off needing its own verified session (old-vs-new store dump + query-output harness on the bench box, scripts at /root/equiv_check2.sh): (a) lower the per-edge cap from 10, (b) skip S5 for names above a lower commonality threshold (currently >50 callables), (c) compute name-fallback candidates lazily at trace time instead of storing them (trace already has the name; an indexed nodes-by-name lookup per low-confidence hop could replace stored rows entirely). Acceptance: no trace/callers output quality loss on the labelled query set, store size and resolve time down.

memories.title: Read paths must order by source position, never raw ids — UUIDv7 + racing parse workers permute results every reindex
memories.body: Node/edge ids are UUIDv7 (insertion-ordered) and parse workers race, so any `ORDER BY ... n.id`/`ed.id` tiebreak — or an implicit order among equal bm25 scores in an FTS pass — returns PERMUTED results after each reindex of an unchanged repo (seen on graphql-platform: partial-class representative flips in search, impls reshuffles, trace chain order changes; 10 diff lines per reindex). Fixed in commit 2630807 by ordering on stable source-position keys (f.path, line/start_byte, dst_name) in trace neighbor expansion + start sets, ftsPass score ties, candidateExactPass, Implementations, Query, and snippet's in-file pick. Guard: TestQueryOutputsStableAcrossIndexOrder indexes one worktree into two stores in OPPOSITE file orders and requires identical outputs — add any new read path's output to it. Acceptance at scale: index the corpus twice fresh, diff the full CLI query-suite outputs — must be byte-identical (harness: /root/equiv_check2.sh on the bench box).

memories.title: Query trust model: upstream tags.scm coverage ratchet + why downloading queries wholesale loses
memories.body: User asked how to trust the hand-written .scm queries vs downloading community ones. Empirical verdict: the canonical upstream tags.scm shipped in tree-sitter-c-sharp v0.23.5 (what GitHub code nav uses) knows ONLY class/interface/method/namespace — no records, structs, enums, delegates, properties, constructors, file-scoped namespaces, attributes, receivers, or bindings; adopting it wholesale would have made the user's record invisible entirely. Trust comes from tests, not provenance. Three layers now: (1) integration suite (compiler-validated fixture, LSP-semantics markers, exact two-way assertions); (2) internal/parse/coverage_test.go — a ratchet that vendors each grammar's own tags.scm (testdata/upstream/, same module version so it's compile-compatible) and asserts every upstream def/ref node type is covered by our query or allowlisted with a written justification (allowlist entries: constraint-clause/type-annotation/bare-type refs → answered by search_content + bindings; exported-constant defs → not in symbol taxonomy); (3) queries compile at NewRegistry against the linked grammar. The ratchet immediately surfaced the same bug class in other languages that C# had: new_expression ctor calls missing in TS/JS (adopted), parenthesized calls in Go (adopted), TS module/function_signature/method_signature/abstract_method_signature defs (adopted), JS assignment-function/object-literal-method/class-expression defs (adopted) — each pinned by adopted_patterns_test.go. On grammar upgrades re-vendor tags.scm so the ratchet tracks upstream learning.

memories.title: LSP cross-check: csharp-ls validates fixture markers; recarto == markers == Roslyn
memories.body: internal/integration/lspcheck_test.go drives the fixture language's REAL language server (manifest lsp_command, csharp: csharp-ls/Roslyn — same engine family as Rider) over a temp copy of the fixture via a minimal JSON-RPC stdio client, asking textDocument/references (includeDeclaration) at every def marker's name token. Bidirectional line-level assertions: (A) every LSP-reported location must be def/ref/tok/implicit-marked (fixture never misses a real usage); (B) every def/ref/implicit line must be LSP-confirmed by some same-named def (fixture never over-claims). Since the main suite proves recarto == markers, the loop closes: recarto == markers == LSP. Mechanics: skip when server not on PATH (hermetic go test); readiness = poll a probe symbol until refs span a second project; respond to server→client requests (workspace/configuration → array of nulls) or the server stalls; namespaces exempt (dotted-name prefix semantics); C# attribute classes fold the Attribute-suffix alias ([Audit] counts for AuditAttribute — note \bAuditAttribute\b grep under-reports attribute usages; find_annotated covers that gap). First run immediately caught: (1) Roslyn reports IMPLICIT references (derived ctor's implicit base() call → counts as RepositoryBase usage with no token on the line) → new `implicit` marker directive models grep's documented blind spot; (2) csharp-ls 0.24 itself MISSES extension-method references whose receiver needs an implicit conversion (circle.IsLarge(), Circle→IShape) → manifest lsp_known_misses with per-entry reason; an entry the server starts reporting fails as stale.

memories.title: Production opencode MCP tool calls (search_graph/search_content) timed out indefinitely; store grew to 2.5GB with an 821MB WAL
memories.body: Production opencode MCP tool calls (search_graph/search_content) timed out indefinitely; store grew to 2.5GB with an 821MB WAL — fix: Five-part fix (commits 558114c..591faa9): durable graph_resolve_pending marker set before first destructive step + missing-index detection folded into the per-query freshness check (one ~65µs round trip, BenchmarkGraphFresh guards it); WriteTx rolls back under context.WithoutCancel; per-index rebuild transactions (resumable); Engine.EnsureFresh — singleflight per-worktree background reconcile detached from the request ctx, 3s bounded wait, stale-served-with-hint on every MCP graph tool, 30s failure cooldown; final wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) after mutating reconciles + token stamp + Stop hook; session-start warm-up hard-bounded at 15s (goroutine abandoned at deadline since git ls-files/FS walks are not ctx-aware); recarto index --force as the manual heal lever for legacy-wedged stores.

memories.title: Cancellation is a first-class failure mode: every cleanup step must run under a detached ctx, every multi-step write must be resumable
memories.body: The production timeout loop exposed a systemic pattern: MCP clients cancel slow requests, and cancellation hits at ARBITRARY points. Three rules now encoded in the codebase: (1) cleanup that must run BECAUSE of cancellation (ROLLBACK in WriteTx) must use context.WithoutCancel — issued with the caller's ctx, database/sql skips it and the pooled connection keeps the open tx (uncommitted reads leak, writers wedge). (2) Long multi-step write sequences (11 CREATE INDEX) must commit per step so a cancellation keeps progress — one shared tx means a per-call timeout can starve the operation forever while bloating the WAL with rolled-back frames each attempt. (3) Any maintenance work a server does on behalf of a request (reconcile/index) must run DETACHED (context.WithoutCancel + singleflight + bounded wait, see Engine.EnsureFresh) so the client's patience bounds only its own wait, never the work. **Why:** test stores are small and never get cancelled mid-flight, so all three bugs stayed invisible until a 2.5GB production store met a 30s client timeout. **How to apply:** when adding any reconcile-path step or background maintenance, ask "what happens if ctx dies right here?" — there are deterministic test seams for this (cancelOnResolvePhase progress, createIndexHook, gated Sources in fresh_test.go).

memories.title: Parser-behavior changes need a graph-wipe migration — hash-based reconcile never re-parses unchanged files
memories.body:
LLM-UX round 1 shipped (12 commits on feature/improve-or-add-features): snippet results carry path; Go type spans include the `type` keyword (parse.go widens single-spec type_declarations, grouped specs stay per-spec); find_references tool (UNION-indexed edge query + word-boundary text sweep, dotted-input narrowed via dst_recv, honest truncation); trace hops is_test + all-test-callers hint; batch get_code_snippet via symbols (≤10, explicit skipped); search_content offset paging (pages the materialized post-per-file-cap order — capped matches need max_per_file, not offset). Closes filed issues 019eb160-aa50… and 019eb160-c5b2….

Key lesson (cost a live bug): Reconcile is content-hash-based, so a parser BEHAVIOR change (recorded spans, names, edges) silently never applies to existing stores — unit tests pass on fresh stores while real stores serve stale data. The fix is the standing migrate.go convention: append a graph-wipe migration (DELETE nodes_fts/nodes_fts_stem/nodes_fts_tri/edge_candidates/type_bindings/edges/nodes/files + meta graph_token:%) and bump schemaVersion (v18 did this). Any future change to internal/parse extraction output needs the same bump — and a live smoke test against an existing store, not just unit tests.

memories.title: Multi-worktree gaps: bulk path drops shared indexes on a populated store; deleted worktrees are never pruned (store grows ~Nx)
memories.body:
Production: user runs 5 git worktrees of one repo → the shared store holds 5 full graph copies (nodes/edges/edge_candidates/FTS all keyed via files.worktree) — a large part of the 2.5GB. Two gaps:

1. BULK GATE IS PER-WORKTREE, SHOULD BE PER-STORE: Reconcile's `bulkLoad := len(have)==0 && len(worklist)>bulkLoadMinFiles` checks only THIS worktree's rows. First index of an added worktree in an already-populated store drops the GLOBAL secondary indexes — every other worktree's queries full-scan for the duration, and the rebuild then runs over N worktrees' rows (cost/benefit flips: the ~40% write win was measured on a truly empty store). Fix: gate also on `SELECT 1 FROM files LIMIT 1` returning nothing (whole store empty), one µs query.

2. NO WORKTREE GC: nothing ever deletes rows for a worktree that no longer exists. Only per-path deleteFile (live worktree, file removed) exists; memory compaction GCs memories only. Deleted worktrees leave their full graph + meta keys (graph_token:<wt>, graph_resolve_pending:<wt>) + sessions rows forever. Fix sketch: prune worktrees not in `git worktree list --porcelain` AND whose path fails os.Stat (both conditions — porcelain is authoritative for this repo's worktrees, stat guards odd cases); cascade via DELETE FROM files WHERE worktree=? (FKs cascade nodes/edges; FTS rows need explicit delete like deleteFile does) + delete meta keys; then checkpoint. Hook: `recarto compact` and/or session-start (gated, best-effort) + explicit `recarto gc`. NOTE: space returns to the OS only after VACUUM (needs ~2x free disk, exclusive); without it the freed pages are just reused.

memories.title: S5 trim: winner-only materialization MUST land together with query-time alternatives in trace (attempt reverted — fixtures pin the contract)
memories.body: Attempted (commit 4816c12, reverted in the next commit): cap S5 emission to the locality-best row — Go resolveNameFallback emit cand[0] only, SQL stratNameFallback rn<=1 — conf still keyed on uncapped count; denormalized dst_node_id provably identical (betterCandidate order == S5 sort). Graph package fully green, but the wider suite caught two REAL contract dependencies on the non-winner rows: (1) internal/integration TestLanguageFixtures/csharp/calls — callers-direction discovery flows THROUGH low-confidence candidate rows (callers InMemoryRepository.Save lost RunStorage→Save because the edge's S5 winner was a different Save; callers(X) needs X anywhere in the edge's top-10, not just #1); (2) internal/cli TestGraphCalleesDedupsIdenticalChains — trace renders an (×N) ambiguity count from multiple candidate rows. So the trim ships ONLY together with query-time alternatives in Engine.callNeighbors (trace.go): after the candidates SQL, synthesize name-fallback candidates in Go for edges whose only/missing candidates are method='name' — callees: rank nodes matching ed.dst_name (idx_nodes_name) with a ranking core SHARED with resolveNameFallback (sameLangFamily + hyper-common>50 skip + sameFile/sameTopDir/path/start/id order + conf by full count, top-10); callers: edges WHERE dst_name=X.name (idx_edges_dstname) lacking strong candidates, include if X in that edge's top-10. Must preserve callNeighbors' per-edge medium-else-low logic, lowCapPerEdge=5, fanout=25, and the (path, line, dst_name, id) output interleaving. Acceptance: the two pinned tests above pass unchanged + s5_winner tests from the reverted commit (recover via `git show 4816c12`). Then: full resolve sheds old rows; recarto compact --vacuum reclaims; expect ~60% store shrink + faster resolve (S5 insert pass was 4.5s on graphql-platform).

memories.title: LLM-UX round 2 shipped: delta tier + get_graph_delta, block-once capture nudge, conflict candidates, CLI parity
memories.body: Round 2 design choices that matter: (1) graph-delta baseline walks back past no-op sessions (sessions whose window journaled no graph_deltas), so /clear or open-close never swallows a delta — the tier persists until a context lived alongside the changes. (2) The capture nudge reaches the MODEL via Stop decision:block (once per session, edits>=3, nothing recorded, stop_hook_active loop-guarded); the human-only systemMessage survives only as the sub-threshold fallback so conversation-heavy low-edit sessions keep a capture prompt. (3) Conflict candidates = findNearDup's middle band [0.25, 0.55) ranked by Jaccard + shared file/symbol refs, advisory on the write path, judged by the recording LLM. (4) Smoke-test gotcha: per-repo stores are keyed by repo path — rm -rf of a smoke worktree does NOT reset its store; reuse poisons session/nudge state. Use a fresh path per smoke run.

memories.title: Review fixes for LLM-UX round 2: nudge-vs-reinforce, prune-vs-baseline, recreate blind spot
memories.body: Three systemic patterns fixed test-first after branch review: (1) any "did this session record anything" check must count reinforcements — Record on a near-dup bumps only updated_at, never created_at, so gate on updated_at >= started_at AND status='active' (archive/supersede/resolve/done bumps are excluded by status; compact-absorb and concurrent-session noise fails quiet, never falsely blocks). (2) graph_deltas retention must clamp its prune cutoff to the current DeltaBaseline — the baseline walk is unbounded across no-op sessions, so a 10th-session horizon alone lets /clear spam erase the very rows the tier still reports. (3) first-index-journals-nothing needs a carve-out: a first index at a path with existing journal rows is a delete-then-recreate (branch switch/stash pop) and must journal "added"; DeltasSince folds disposition from first/last events (first!=added → existed at baseline, last!=removed → exists now; removed→added reads as changed). Renames stay a documented blind spot (removals at old path). Also: refConflicts needs ORDER BY updated_at DESC for deterministic cap survivors; SQLite DISTINCT+ORDER BY requires the sort column in the result set.

memories.title: Claude hooks pin PowerShell shell on Windows installs
memories.body:
Claude Code hook command entries support an optional `shell` field ("bash" default | "powershell"). On Windows, Claude launches command hooks via Git Bash (else PowerShell), which breaks `recarto hook …`, so the claudecode installer now pins `"shell":"powershell"` per hook entry on Windows only.

Implementation: `hookSpec` carries a `shell` field; `hookSpecs` fills it from `hookShell()`, which returns "powershell" when `goos == "windows"` else "". `goos` is a package var indirecting `runtime.GOOS` so tests override it. `appendHook` takes a shell arg and omits the field when empty. `ownedCommands` now returns command→shell (not a set), and `syncHooks` compares command+shell, so re-running init on an older Windows install (commands present but no shell) re-syncs to add the shell instead of reporting "already present".

memories.title: Performance is a gated requirement because Recarto runs in Claude hooks
memories.body:
The user requires that retrieval/indexing changes be proven to not degrade SPEED, not just quality — because Recarto runs inside Claude Code lifecycle hooks where latency is user-visible.

**Why:** SessionStart injection, PostRead/PostEdit reconcile + bug surfacing, and MCP query tools all run synchronously in the agent's hook path; a slowdown is felt on every turn.

**How to apply:** The eval gate (internal/eval, see the archex-net-wins design spec) tracks a performance dimension alongside recall@10/MRR/zero-hit:
- Indexing: full index + incremental reconcile (PostEdit hot path).
- Querying: SearchGuided/search_graph p50/p95, plus get_code_snippet.
- Hook entry points: SessionStart injection time, PostEdit reconcile time, each with a budget target.
- Two signal types: deterministic work-counters (FTS queries/search, symbols re-resolved/edit, allocs/op, ns/op) hard-gated in normal `go test ./...` (machine-independent); wall-clock timings measured on a DEDICATED PERF VM (stable hardware → tight tolerances), via a portable `recarto eval perf` lane with a committed perf-baseline.
- Process: run `recarto eval perf` on the VM before merging any retrieval (Phase C) change and record the delta; the switch-rule ADR makes this a required pre-merge step. No degradations accepted in quality OR speed.

memories.body:
A dedicated VM is available for the wall-clock perf lane (the `recarto eval perf` / ADR-001 step that must run on stable hardware, not shared CI).

- Bare image: install toolchain each time — `apt-get install -y build-essential ca-certificates git`, and copy the version-matched Go toolchain (tar `go env GOROOT` → /usr/local/go) since apt has no Go 1.26.4. Build with PATH=/usr/local/go/bin:$PATH GOTOOLCHAIN=local CGO_ENABLED=1.
