- Seed/compare: `recarto eval perf --repo internal/eval/testdata/corpus --queries internal/eval/testdata/queries.json --perf-baseline internal/eval/testdata/perf_baseline.json`.
- Reference seed on this VM (committed): index_full≈177ms, warm_reconcile≈0.3ms, query_p50≈0.89ms, query_p95≈1.27ms; stable across runs. Re-seed on THIS VM only (per-host comparability).

memories.title: graph.OutlineSymbol has no Path field; topDir already taken in resolve.go
memories.body:
Two gotchas hit while building B2 impact.go (internal/graph):

1) graph.OutlineSymbol (internal/graph/outline.go:11) has NO Path field — Engine.Outline is scoped to a single path argument, so the path is the query input, not on the struct. Code that resolves "which file defined this symbol" from an Outline result set must track the path separately (e.g. map qualified_name->path by re-walking the changed paths with Outline). The Phase B B2 plan's affectedFrom snippet assumed d.Path existed; it does not.

2) topDir is ALREADY declared in internal/graph/resolve.go:717 (returns the leading segment WITH trailing slash, e.g. "a/", and "" for root files — used for the SQL same-top-dir locality tiebreak). A new helper that returns "a" (no slash) / "." must use a different name (I used topDirSegment) or it redeclares. Grep internal/graph for a helper name before adding one.

memories.title: Local env indexes ~1.5× slower than the perf VM — eval perf gives false index_full regressions here
memories.body:
The assistant's working environment (Claude Code sandbox for recarto) is NOT the dedicated perf VM and indexes ~1.5× slower than it. Running `recarto eval perf --repo internal/eval/testdata/corpus --queries internal/eval/testdata/queries.json` locally reports `index_full_ms` ≈ 258–265ms vs the VM-seeded baseline of 177ms (a false +45% "REGRESSION"), while warm_reconcile/query_p50/query_p95 stay within tolerance.

This is a HARDWARE artifact, not a real regression: the full-index code path (graph.New → Reconcile → IndexFile → parse → Resolve → store writes) is unchanged by Phase B (verified via `git diff master..HEAD` — only B5's WorktreeHead and B4's parse.Registry read-methods touched those packages, neither on the index write path). index_full_ms is the most hardware-sensitive metric (CPU-bound tree-sitter parse + SQLite writes), so it inflates on a slower/noisier box.

Takeaway: per ADR-001, the wall-clock `recarto eval perf` gate MUST run on the dedicated perf VM (stable hardware). Do NOT trust local `eval perf` index_full numbers and do NOT re-seed perf_baseline.json from this environment. `eval perf` compares against an existing baseline and only seeds when the baseline file is absent (so a local run is non-destructive).

memories.title: C1 BM25F: FTS5 bm25 weights are positional over ALL columns incl. UNINDEXED; tiny corpora have degenerate IDF
memories.body:
Phase C / C1 (BM25F per-field weighting) landed on `feature/archex-features` (commit 105baff). `internal/graph/search.go` now weights the `name` column 3x above `qualified_name` via `bm25(table, 0.0, w_name, w_qual)` in `ftsPass` (helper `bm25Expr(table)`; nodes_fts/nodes_fts_stem weighted, nodes_fts_tri single-column stays plain). `bm25NameWeight=3.0, bm25QualWeight=1.0`.

Two non-obvious facts verified empirically this session:

1. **FTS5 `bm25()` weight args are positional over EVERY column, including `UNINDEXED` ones.** nodes_fts is `(node_id UNINDEXED, name, qualified_name)`, so weighting name/qual requires a LEADING 0.0 for node_id: `bm25(t, 0.0, w_name, w_qual)`. Proof: `bm25(t,0,1,5)` vs `bm25(t,0,5,1)` flips name-vs-qualified order. If you omit the node_id slot the weights bind to the wrong columns.

2. **On tiny corpora bm25 IDF collapses to ~0, so per-field weighting has NO effect** — a term appearing in ~all docs has idf≈log(1)=0, and 0*weight=0; order falls to the rowid/path tie-break. A 7-doc unit test showed all-zero scores; adding ~30 filler symbols (so the term is RARE) restored real IDF and the weighting reordered as expected. Lesson for ranking unit tests: include enough distractor symbols that the query term is rare, else the test is blind. Mechanism guard: `TestBM25FNameOutranksQualifiedSegment` (needs weight >= 3 to lift a leaf-name match above 4 namespace-segment matches).

Evidence C1 is a net win with no regression: tuning fixture (queries.json) UNCHANGED (no name-vs-qual case → baseline.json NOT ratcheted, gate stays green); HELD-OUT set lexical-control MRR 0.542→0.667 (+0.125, semantic unchanged) — a genuine non-overfit gain. Recall/zero-hit unchanged. VM wall-clock (root@<perf-vm>): index_full steady-state 174-176ms ≈ baseline 177ms (first run 222ms is cold-cache warmup — discard it; take the median of N), query p50/p95 within tolerance. C1 only reorders already-matching rows so recall is mathematically preserved.

memories.title: C2 ships suppress-only (broadenCeil=1.0); AvgIDF (C2.4) skipped — no-regression over unvalidated gain
memories.body:
Phase C / C2 (confidence-gated broadener fusion) on `feature/archex-features`. `internal/graph/confidence.go` + `lexicalSearch` scale the porter/synonym/trigram fusion weights by `broadenGain(coeffVar(primaryScores), jaccardTopK(primary, stem, limit))`, bounded `[broadenFloor=0.5, broadenCeil=1.0]`.

Two deliberate scope decisions, both driven by the user's "no regressions" + evidence-backed values:

1. **Suppress-only (broadenCeil = 1.0).** The spec's design is symmetric — suppress broadeners when the exact pass is confident (precision) AND amplify them when scores are flat (recall). I shipped only the suppress arm. Rationale: with ceil=1.0 a broadener NEVER exceeds its original fixed weight, so C2 is provably recall-safe vs the pre-C2 baseline (it can only reduce broadener noise, never amplify it). The amplify arm (ceil>1) is the only part that could inject noise, and it showed ZERO measured benefit on the fixture — the fixture's flat-score underfill queries are token-disjoint semantic misses (e.g. "Suspend", "Enqueue") that no amount of broadening reaches. The lean-in arm is a documented one-const future change, gated on a corpus that proves it helps.

2. **AvgIDF (plan task C2.4) skipped entirely.** The spec lists AvgIDF as a "dependency-free pre-retrieval broaden-now signal." It needs per-term doc-frequency via an fts5vocab query — i.e. an EXTRA SQL query on every search, in the Claude-hook hot path. Since C2 is already gate-neutral and recall-safe, AvgIDF would add hook-path latency for no measured quality gain → skipped per YAGNI + the no-speed-regression mandate. CV + Jaccard are computed from in-memory results (no extra SQL).

Evidence: gate green (no regression), fixture + held-out both unchanged (0.889/0.536, 0.667/0.667), alloc budget unchanged, VM query p50/p95 within tolerance (no latency cost from the in-memory confidence work). The gain is ACTIVE though (observed 0.5–1.0 across fixture underfill queries), so it's not dead code — just a precision optimization the small fixture's rank-1 targets don't surface as MRR movement, hence baseline.json was NOT ratcheted.

memories.title: Resolve-phase profile on graphql-platform (2-CPU VM): measured hot spots + validated levers
memories.body:
Reproduced the user-reported "resolving references very slow" on graphql-platform@6d25fa3 (10,115 files, 130k nodes, 521k edges, 370k call edges, 1.24M candidates, 766MB store) on a 2-CPU/4GB Linux VM: first-index resolve phase = 5m19s; full re-resolve (TestResolveBenchProfile) = 6m05s. NOT Windows-specific — the dedicated fast benchmark box had hidden it (whole DB in OS cache).

Measured step times (re-resolve, baseline → +cache_size(-131072)+temp_store(2) → +foreign_keys OFF), digest byte-identical across all three (965375ca...8445):
- clear candidates DELETE (1.24M rows): 57.6s → 22.3s → 2.2s (FK-child status defeats SQLite's truncate optimization; with FK off it kicks in)
- clear dst_node_id UPDATE (262k rows): 50.6s → 30.7s → 4.4s (edges' FK machinery ~100µs/row even when setting NULL)
- S1-S4: 27.0s → 12.3s → 8.8s
- S5 name fallback (948,606 inserts via per-row prepared Exec): 48.6s → 52.7s → 34.0s (I/O-insensitive; cost = database/sql+VDBE per row + 2 FK parent probes; ~36µs/row remains)
- denormalize: 75.4s → 34.2s → 32.3s (dominated by the 1.58M-row Go-side scans, esp. 1.07M edge_candidates rows)
- rebuild idx_edge_candidates_dst: 28.2s → 13.8s → 7.6s
- TOTAL: 6m4.8s → 4m7.1s → 3m4.1s
Also: S6 stratImplicitCtor = 56.5s (167,912 rows; NOT in the bench harness — it drifted) and FK on/off makes NO difference to S6: its cost is the per-pair NOT-EXISTS probe into the 1M-row candidates PK + materialized join, fixable by driving from a precomputed unresolved-edge temp table. ANALYZE(analysis_limit=1000) = 4.4s, not sub-second, at this scale.

Root causes: (1) SQLite defaults — 2MB page cache (SQLITE_DEFAULT_CACHE_SIZE=-2000) and file-backed temp store (SQLITE_TEMP_STORE=1) — while resolve churns a ~1M-row random-UUID candidate btree in one giant tx; (2) FK enforcement paying 2 parent probes/insert and defeating the truncate DELETE; (3) per-row Go↔driver round-trips in S5/denormalize. End-to-end first index with just the two pragmas: resolve 5m19s → 3m22s, candidate counts byte-identical per method. PRAGMA foreign_keys must be set OUTSIDE a transaction (no-op inside) — a scoped FK-off must wrap BEGIN...COMMIT on the same conn and restore after.

memories.title: temp_store=MEMORY scoped to WriteTxBulk, not global DSN (VACUUM OOM)
memories.body:
A global `temp_store(2)` DSN pragma is an OOM hazard: `recarto compact --vacuum` runs a bare VACUUM on a pooled connection, and VACUUM's transient database can be as large as the whole store (10GB+ reported). With a global in-memory temp store that transient DB is built in RAM. Fix: keep `temp_store` off the DSN (modernc's SQLITE_TEMP_STORE=1 → on-disk default) and apply `PRAGMA temp_store=MEMORY` only inside `applyBulkProfile` (WriteTxBulk), whose temp size is bounded by edge/candidate counts. Resolve runs in WriteTxBulk so it keeps the in-memory-temp win; VACUUM and every other pooled connection stay on disk.

Also: WriteTxBulk profile setup/restore must route EVERY post-mutation failure path through a single restore-then-discard helper (`restoreOrDiscard`) — never roll a pragma back inline while ignoring that rollback's error, or a mis-profiled (128 MiB cache / FK-off / MEMORY-temp) connection can leak back to the pool. Capture prior cache_size AND temp_store and restore the captured values, not presumed defaults.

memories.title: Corruption recovery design: build-aside salvage + swap, pool flush via SetConnMaxLifetime (no Store.DB pointer swap)
memories.body: For the "database disk image is malformed (11)" record_memory failure: recovery is planned as a store-level build-aside repair — salvage precious tables (meta minus graph_token:%, memories, memory_refs, memory_minhash, counters, sessions, memory_tombstones, memory_sync_outbox, memory_sync_merges) from the live corrupt DB (WAL applied) into a fresh migrated tmp DB, rebuild memories_fts from memories.search_text, leave graph tables empty (lazy reconcile rebuilds), integrity_check the tmp, then quarantine-rename the corrupt files and swap the tmp in. Runtime (serve) recovery must NOT swap the Store.DB pointer (~90 direct .DB accesses across ~40 files would race); instead keep the same *sql.DB and flush its pool with SetConnMaxLifetime(1ns)+SetMaxIdleConns(0) after the file swap so new conns open the new file at the same path. Multi-process repairs are serialized with an O_EXCL lockfile next to store.db. Open-time path: auto-repair when Ping/Migrate return a corrupt error, plus a stamped (24h) PRAGMA quick_check for serve startup because a corrupt DB can open and read fine (the reported repro).

memories.title: record_memory fails with "database disk image is malformed (11)" while read tools (search_graph, get_code_snippet) keep working all session
memories.body: record_memory fails with "database disk image is malformed (11)" while read tools (search_graph, get_code_snippet) keep working all session — fix: Added store.IsCorrupt (driver result code via errors.As on *sqlite.Error, extended codes masked; message fallback) and store.Repair: a build-aside salvage that copies the precious tables (meta minus graph_token:%, memories, memory_refs, memory_minhash, counters, sessions, memory_tombstones, memory_sync_outbox, memory_sync_merges, graph_deltas) into a freshly migrated temp DB, rebuilds memories_fts for ACTIVE rows only, verifies + checkpoints + re-verifies on a fresh connection, then quarantines the damaged file set to store.db.corrupt-<ts> and swaps in the replacement. Triggers: reactive at store.Open, proactive via store.WithQuickCheck (serve/sync-server/feedback handler, rate-limited by a <path>.quickcheck sidecar), and `recarto repair` dispatched before app.Open. writeTx wraps a corrupt write with actionable guidance rather than repairing under a live pool — Store.DB is read directly by unsynchronised callers across ~40 files, so renaming a WAL-mode DB out from under active connections is unsafe. RECARTO_AUTO_REPAIR=0 disables automatic repair.

memories.title: Mid-session corruption heal: rebuild the whole App at the MCP addTool choke point, not a Store-level pool swap
memories.body: Field bug: graph tools (get_code_snippet, search_content's background refresh) failed all session with raw "database disk image is malformed (11)" because open-time repair (b2a0e7b/e3cc3f8) only fires when prepare() fails, and the quick_check stamp throttles the proactive check for 24h — a store corrupted after its last passing check serves broken graph queries for up to a day with no heal and no actionable message. Architect decision: do NOT hot-swap inside store.Store (Store.DB is a public *sql.DB read at ~91 unsynchronised call sites — pointer swap is a data race). Instead heal at the MCP layer: addTool/addToolSchema are the single choke point for all 20 tools; wrap them with an appHolder (RWMutex) that on store.IsCorrupt(err) closes the whole App, runs store.VerifyAndRepair per store path, reopens app.Open(cfg) and retries once. Requires graph.Engine background refreshes to become cancellable (they use context.WithoutCancel today, so app.Close can't drain them — a Windows rename blocker). Also: writeTx must remove the .quickcheck stamp on corrupt classification so other processes re-check at next open. Files: internal/mcp/server.go, internal/store/store.go, internal/graph/fresh.go.
